question: How many types of writs can be issued by the Supreme Court of India for the protection of Fundamental Rights?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Five.__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The Supreme Court of India is the defender of the fundamental rights of the citizens. For that, it has original and wide powers.
 
• It issues **five** kinds of writs for enforcing the fundamental rights of the citizens.
 
• **Writs:__**
 __
 
• ​Writs are a written order from the Supreme Court or High Court that commands constitutional remedies for Indian Citizens against the violation of their fundamental rights.
 
• **Article 32** in the Indian Constitution deals with constitutional remedies that an Indian citizen can seek from the Supreme Court of India and the High Court against the violation of his/her fundamental rights. 
 
• The same **article** gives the Supreme Court power to issue writs for the enforcement of rights whereas the High Court has the same power under **Article 226.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are** five types** of Writs which are:

 
 
• ​Habeas Corpus.
 
• Mandamus.
 
• Certiorari.
 
• Quo Warranto.
 
• Prohibition.
 
 
 
• ​ All these writs are an effective method of enforcing the rights of the people and compelling the authorities to fulfill the duties which are bound to perform under the law.
